it's not that the researchers aren't smart

they're very smart, and i believe well-intentioned

however, they overestimate their own ability to predict individual and market responses in complex environments

and it's not the first time. when EIP-1559 was being pitched, top researchers presented it as burning insane amounts of ETH, turning ETH into a hyper-deflationary asset

when logic suggested that as fees go up, market participants would find alternatives, and thus burn would only modestly reduce net-issuance at best

changing the issuance curve is frankly a lot more complex than that, especially given the shape of activity on Ethereum today

tweets.text:
my take is that:

1) issuance is already very, very low for ETH. lower than BTC, lower than almost every other blockchain, and lower than the supply of new gold added to the market every year
2) issuance is not a primary driver of ETH price at these already low levels. demand to hold ETH as a speculative SoV and use ETH for exchange and productive purposes drives ETH price. and like it or not, staking yield has become a key factor for why people choose to buy and (crucially) hold ETH
3) consistency and predictability in ETH's issuance policy is more important to creating market confidence around ETH (and by extension, Ethereum) than perfectly optimizing issuance
4) solo/small stakers shouldn't be allowed to be priced out of the market, because if shit really ever hits the fan, you're going to need them
5) we should focus on scaling Ethereum as a network, drive much more use to the network, charge appropriate fees to use it, and allow fee burn to continue to offset some amount of the already low issuance

one of the less obvious things about smart phones is how they have dramatically changed computing habits

but it's more than just having a computer with you everywhere you go

the small form factor has dramatically changed the types of content we consume and interact with

further, you can only have one app displayed at a time for normal use

social media apps optimized content for that form factor and won the internet as a result (in addition to providing unending dopamine)

and the only thing which can break us out now is a shift to unconstrained augmented reality (AR) interfaces
